title: Lesson 25: Capstone: Plan and Scope a Complete Intermediate Engagement
description: The closing capstone: plan and scope a complete intermediate engagement by producing three composed artifacts, a scope statement, a plan, and a defensible estimate, against a fixed calendar and budget.

questions.question: For the Linehaul engagement, why is the duplicate-lane cleanup best treated as an exclusion rather than absorbed into the build?
options: Cleaning the spreadsheet is faster than building the matching logic, so folding it in cuts the schedule
The duplicates are a data governance problem that predates the project, so the system must be correct on clear rows and loud on ambiguous ones rather than inheriting the cleanup
Deleting the duplicate rows improves the golden set but has no effect on the matching behavior
The rate director prefers the duplicates stay so the spreadsheet stays the single source of truth
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that the duplicates are a client-owned data governance problem you name with evidence and refuse to own, pricing around it: the system must be correct on clear rows and loud on ambiguous ones. This makes the exclusion load-bearing rather than optional.

questions.question: Where does the lesson say buffers belong in the plan, and why?
options: One large buffer at the final week so the estimate has room at the very end
At the end of the calendar only, to absorb any overdue work in a single recovery zone
In small, positioned amounts where uncertainty actually lives, such as after the extract-schema spike, after the first golden-set evaluation, and before handover
Distributed evenly across all eight weeks regardless of risk
questions.explanation: The lesson argues that a single end-of-plan buffer moves all risk to the final week, where it cannot be recovered, so the intermediate habit is small buffers placed at the points of real uncertainty.

questions.question: Which property makes the scope, plan, and estimate a single composed artifact rather than three separate documents?
options: Each phase covers one lifecycle phase and each document uses the same clients

Each artifact strengthens the others: scope provides the testable gates the plan schedules, the plan places buffers where the estimate's risks live, and the estimate names the assumptions the scope survives
All three are written on the same day before any discovery happens
Each document has an equal word count and a corresponding endnote
questions.explanation: The lesson's composition test is interdependence: if you can delete one artifact without weakening the other two, they are stacked, not composed. Scope feeds the plan's gates, the plan prices the estimate, and the estimate names the assumptions scope must survive.
